title: ABG: acid–base reading

findings.where: Images 1, 7, 9 and 15; expected-compensation panel; abg.jsx RULES respiratory equations
findings.title: Respiratory equations do not clearly scope the coefficient or sign
findings.problem: “24 − 2 (acute) or 5 (chronic) × …” does not unambiguously apply the subtraction and multiplication to both alternatives. The respiratory-acidosis equation has the same grouping defect. Students copying these as standalone equations can calculate the wrong bicarbonate. For example, at PaCO₂ 20, the intended respiratory-alkalosis estimates are 20 acute and 14 chronic.
findings.fix: Write HCO₃⁻ ≈ 24 + k × ((PaCO₂ − 40) / 10), with k = 1 acute or 4 chronic; and HCO₃⁻ ≈ 24 − k × ((40 − PaCO₂) / 10), with k = 2 acute or 5 chronic. Retain ±2 and the units.

findings.where: Step 'limits' caption and narration versus images 7 and 15 and compensationLimit('metabolic', 'alkalosis')
findings.title: Following the narration can disagree with the computed verdict
findings.problem: The caption and narration teach only PaCO₂ ≈ 0.7 × HCO₃⁻ + 21 ±2, but the interpreter accepts either of two formulas. This changes actual decisions. With pH 7.50, PaCO₂ 53 and HCO₃⁻ 40, the narrated rule gives 47–51 mmHg, placing 53 outside expected compensation. The interpreter accepts 47–53.2 and returns partially compensated metabolic alkalosis without a mixed-disorder caution. These values are internally consistent.
findings.fix: Make the caption and recording acknowledge both accepted formulas and their differing estimates, or standardize the displayed teaching and interpreter on one sourced convention. Add this value set as a cross-modal regression test.

assessment: Needs revision: the printed respiratory equations are ambiguous, and the narrated metabolic-alkalosis rule does not match the interpreter's accepted range.
